# Switch

A labeled on/off switch on the Field contract, with the label to its right: pass `label`, and `checked` with `onCheckedChange` (or `defaultChecked`). Clicking the label or pressing Space flips it; the thumb slides with the theme spring and stretches while pressed. With `name`, a switch that is on submits `name=value` with its form.

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/switch/switch";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Switch label="Wi-Fi" checked={wifi} onCheckedChange={setWifi} />
<Switch label="Nightly backups" name="backups" description="At 2 a.m." defaultChecked />
```

## Usage

Use it for a setting that takes effect at once.

## Use instead when

- Use `Checkbox` instead for a choice that applies when a form is submitted, such as accepting terms.

## Props

Type: `SwitchProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  | Whether it is on, for a controlled switch; pair it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-4`, `col-span-2`). Appearance classes warn in development; style switches in your theme. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  | Whether it starts on, for an uncontrolled switch. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the label, read after it through `aria-describedby`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the switch and fades it. |
| `error` | `ErrorMessages` |  | What is wrong, from your server action or client check, shown under the label; the switch gets `aria-invalid`. A message is text or a React node (one with a link); an empty string or array means valid. |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually; screen readers still read it as the switch's name. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The setting it turns on, shown to the right of the switch and read as its name. Required: every control needs a name. To hide it visually, keep it and add `hideLabel`. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The form field name it submits under when on. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `((checked: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with the new state when it turns on or off. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Shows the state but ignores clicks and keys, unlike `disabled`, which also fades it. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | The track element, a `<span role="switch">`. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | The switch must be on to submit the form: it gets `required` and `aria-required`, and the label a marker. |
| `value` | `string` |  | What it submits when on (`on` without one). |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `defaultValue`: Not a prop. A switch's starting state is `defaultChecked`: `<Switch defaultChecked>`.
- `errorMessage`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `error`: `<Switch error="Required.">`.
- `helperText`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `description`: `<Switch description="...">`.
- `invalid`: Not a prop. `error` marks the switch invalid: `<Switch error="What is wrong">`.
- `isChecked`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `checked`: `<Switch checked={on}>`.
- `isDisabled`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `disabled`: `<Switch disabled>`.
- `isInvalid`: Not a prop. `error` marks the switch invalid: `<Switch error="What is wrong">`.
- `isRequired`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `required`: `<Switch required>`.
- `onChange`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `onCheckedChange`, which gets the new state: `onCheckedChange={setOn}`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `ErrorMessage`

One error message: text, or a React element for a message that carries a link or other markup.

```ts
type ErrorMessage = string | ReactElement;
```

### `ErrorMessages`

What an `error` prop or a `Form` `errors` value takes: one message, or several as an array.

```ts
type ErrorMessages = ErrorMessage | ErrorMessage[];
```
